record.context_brief: Extend perfectness and simplicity criteria for PE(V)
record.original_question: Determine whether the two theorems cited from [Lo5] continue to hold for broader classes of Jordan pairs: namely, whether PE(V) is perfect exactly when V has no simple factors isomorphic to (F2, F2), (F3, F3), or (H2(F2), H2(F2)), and whether PE(V) is simple exactly when V is simple and avoids those exceptional factors.

evidence.quote: The problem is to find out if these two theorems of [Lo5] hold for more general Jordan pairs. It follows from (b) that is natural to assume simplicity of V for the second theorem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let V = (V⁺, V⁻) be a Jordan pair, and let L(V) denote its Tits–Kantor–Koecher Lie algebra. The projective elementary group PE(V) is defined as the subgroup of Aut(L(V)) generated by the one-parameter subgroups exp(ad x) for x ∈ V⁺ and x ∈ V⁻. A Jordan pair V is called simple if it has no nonzero proper ideals and its product is nonzero; the simple factors of V are the simple Jordan pairs occurring in a decomposition of V. Distinguish three "exceptional" simple Jordan pairs: (F₂, F₂), (F₃, F₃), and (H₂(F₂), H₂(F₂)) (where Hₙ(F) denotes the Jordan pair of n×n hermitian matrices over F).

Two known theorems for finite-dimensional Jordan pairs over a field state:
(T1) PE(V) is a perfect group if and only if V has no simple factor isomorphic to (F₂, F₂), (F₃, F₃), or (H₂(F₂), H₂(F₂));
(T2) PE(V) is a simple group if and only if V is simple and not isomorphic to any of those three exceptional Jordan pairs.

Problem: Determine whether (T1) and (T2) extend to broader classes of Jordan pairs (for instance, infinite-dimensional Jordan pairs, or Jordan pairs over arbitrary commutative rings). Specifically, prove or disprove that for the broader class under consideration:
(a) PE(V) is perfect ⇔ V has no simple factor isomorphic to (F₂, F₂), (F₃, F₃), or (H₂(F₂), H₂(F₂));
(b) Assuming V is simple, PE(V) is simple ⇔ V is not isomorphic to any of (F₂, F₂), (F₃, F₃), or (H₂(F₂), H₂(F₂)).
artifact.category_tag: Jordan pairs and projective elementary groups
artifact.status_search_result: The classical perfectness and simplicity theorems for PE(V) are due to Loos for finite-dimensional Jordan pairs, and Loos–Neher have developed Steinberg groups and simplicity results for elementary groups defined by Jordan pairs graded by 3-graded root systems, recovering analogous statements with the same exceptional factors. However, no source verified definitively settles the extension of both theorems to fully general Jordan pairs, so the status is taken to be unknown / partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: Steinberg groups and simplicity of elementary groups defined by Jordan pairs
status_evidence.snippet: With exactly 3 exceptions over the Galois fields F2 and F3, the projective elementary group PE(V) is simple.
status_evidence.claim: Loos–Neher establish simplicity of PE(V) up to the same three exceptional Jordan pairs in a broader setting via Steinberg groups.

status_evidence.title: Steinberg groups for Jordan pairs (Loos–Neher)
status_evidence.snippet: Projective elementary group PE(V) defined for an arbitrary Jordan pair V; Φ-commutator relations from a 3-graded root system.
status_evidence.claim: PE(V) is defined for arbitrary Jordan pairs and studied via Steinberg-type presentations, suggesting partial extensions of the perfectness/simplicity criteria.
